110	class DriverFingerprintStore:
111	    """SQLite-backed own-DB store of :class:`FingerprintCell` rows.
112	
113	    Table ``driver_fingerprint_cells``: primary key ``cell_key`` (``NOT NULL``), plus the
114	    six ``CellAddress`` identity columns, the fitted ``mean``/``sigma``/``support_n``/
115	    ``shared_floor_applied`` payload, ``status`` (``"resolved"``/``"unresolved"``), and
116	    ``format_version``.
117	    """
118	
119	    def __init__(self, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH, *, must_exist: bool = False) -> None:
120	        """Construct the store, creating the schema on first use.
121	
122	        must_exist:
123	            When True, raise ``FileNotFoundError`` if ``db_path`` does not already exist,
124	            BEFORE any connect/schema work -- a read-only construction mode (mirrors
125	            ``ReferenceUtilizationStore``/``GripStore``).
126	        """
127	        if must_exist and not Path(db_path).exists():
128	            raise FileNotFoundError(db_path)
129	        self.db_path = db_path
130	        self._init_schema()
131	
132	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ schema
133	    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
134	        con = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
135	        con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
136	        return con
137	
138	    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
139	        parent = Path(self.db_path).parent
140	        if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
141	            parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
142	        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}" TEXT NOT NULL' if c == "cell_key" else f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
143	        with self._connect() as con:
144	            con.execute(
145	                f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}, "
146	                f'PRIMARY KEY ("cell_key"))'
147	            )
148	            self._migrate_missing_columns(con)
149	
150	    def _migrate_missing_columns(self, con: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
151	        """ALTER-add any expected column absent from an existing table (additive only).
152	
153	        Mirrors the house pattern exactly: a DB created before a new nullable column was
154	        added keeps loading -- the ADD COLUMN backfills existing rows with NULL rather than
155	        crashing the query. Never drops or renames.
156	        """
157	        existing = {row[1] for row in con.execute("PRAGMA table_info(driver_fingerprint_cells)")}
158	        for c in _COLUMNS:
159	            if c not in existing:
160	                con.execute(f'ALTER TABLE driver_fingerprint_cells ADD COLUMN "{c}"')
161	
162	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ guards
163	    def _check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(self, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary) -> None:
164	        if era != vocabulary.rules_era:
165	            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
166	                f"era={era!r} does not match vocabulary.rules_era={vocabulary.rules_era!r} "
167	                f"(vocabulary_id={vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r}) -- refusing rather than "
168	                f"silently choosing one"
169	            )
170	
171	    def _check_no_vocabulary_drift(
172	        self, con: sqlite3.Connection, driver: str, era: str, channel: str, what_measure: str,
173	        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
174	    ) -> None:
175	        existing = {
176	            row[0]
177	            for row in con.execute(
178	                "SELECT DISTINCT vocabulary_version FROM driver_fingerprint_cells "
179	                "WHERE driver=? AND era=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
180	                (driver, era, channel, what_measure),
181	            )
182	        }
183	        stale = existing - {vocabulary.vocabulary_id}
184	        if stale:
185	            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
186	                f"driver={driver!r} era={era!r} channel={channel!r} what_measure={what_measure!r} "
187	                f"already has stored cells under vocabulary_version(s) {sorted(stale)!r} -- "
188	                f"refusing to write under a different vocabulary_version "
189	                f"{vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r} without an explicit migration"
190	            )
191	
192	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write
193	    def write_fingerprint(
194	        self,
195	        driver: str,
196	        era: str,
197	        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
198	        channel: str,
199	        what_measure: str,
200	        observations: Mapping[str, CellObservation],
201	        *,
202	        allow_unverified: bool = False,
203	    ) -> None:
204	        """Write EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` rows, one per ``vocabulary.class_ids``.
205	
206	        A class absent from ``observations``, or whose ``support_n`` is below the
207	        pre-registered unresolved-support floor, is written as ``status="unresolved"``
208	        (``NULL`` mean/sigma) -- never a missing row. ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` on the
209	        non-NULL ``cell_key`` primary key makes a rerun idempotent (replace-on-rerun):
210	        re-writing the same fingerprint never accumulates duplicate rows.
211	        """
212	        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
213	        if what_measure in RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES:
214	            raise ReservedWhatMeasureError(
215	                f"what_measure={what_measure!r} is a reserved (Build-2, dormant) slot -- "
216	                f"the store refuses to populate it in Build 1"
217	            )
218	        vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)
219	
220	        placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in _COLUMNS)
221	        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
222	        sql = f"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}) VALUES ({placeholders})"
223	
224	        rows: list[tuple] = []
225	        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
226	            obs = observations.get(class_id)
227	            support_n = obs.support_n if obs is not None else None
228	            is_resolved = (
229	                obs is not None
230	                and support_n is not None
231	                and support_n >= _UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR
232	            )
233	            address = CellAddress(
234	                driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
235	                class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
236	            )
237	            rows.append(
238	                (
239	                    address.cell_key, driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, class_id, channel,
240	                    what_measure,
241	                    (obs.mean if is_resolved else None),
242	                    (obs.sigma if is_resolved else None),
243	                    support_n,
244	                    (_RESOLVED if is_resolved else _UNRESOLVED),
245	                    (obs.shared_floor_applied if obs is not None else None),
246	                    FORMAT_VERSION,
247	                )
248	            )
249	
250	        with self._connect() as con:
251	            self._check_no_vocabulary_drift(con, driver, era, channel, what_measure, vocabulary)
252	            con.executemany(sql, rows)
253	
254	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ reads
255	    def get_fingerprint(
256	        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
257	    ) -> list[FingerprintCell]:
258	        """Return EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` cells -- never fits, never omits a class.
259	
260	        A class with no stored row is synthesized as an ``"unresolved"`` cell purely by
261	        enumerating ``vocabulary.class_ids`` -- no observation is read, no value is
262	        computed. This is the NO-fit-on-read guarantee: a miss is a placeholder, not a
263	        trigger.
264	        """
265	        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
266	        with self._connect() as con:
267	            rows = con.execute(
268	                "SELECT * FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
269	                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
270	                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
271	            ).fetchall()
272	        by_class = {r["class_id"]: r for r in rows}
273	
274	        cells: list[FingerprintCell] = []
275	        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
276	            row = by_class.get(class_id)
277	            if row is None:
278	                cells.append(
279	                    FingerprintCell(
280	                        driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
281	                        class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
282	                        mean=None, sigma=None, support_n=None, status=_UNRESOLVED,
283	                        shared_floor_applied=None, format_version=FORMAT_VERSION,
284	                    )
285	                )
286	            else:
287	                cells.append(
288	                    FingerprintCell(
289	                        driver=row["driver"], era=row["era"], vocabulary_version=row["vocabulary_version"],
290	                        class_id=row["class_id"], channel=row["channel"], what_measure=row["what_measure"],
291	                        mean=row["mean"], sigma=row["sigma"], support_n=row["support_n"],
292	                        status=row["status"], shared_floor_applied=row["shared_floor_applied"],
293	                        format_version=row["format_version"],
294	                    )
295	                )
296	        return cells
297	
298	    def row_count(
299	        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
300	    ) -> int:
301	        """Number of stored rows for this (driver,era,vocab,channel,what_measure) slot.
302	
303	        Diagnostic -- used by idempotency tests to confirm a rerun never accumulates
304	        duplicate rows (expected to equal ``vocabulary.k`` after any number of rewrites).
305	        """
306	        with self._connect() as con:
307	            cur = con.execute(
308	                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
309	                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
310	                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
311	            )
312	            return int(cur.fetchone()[0])
313

  disagree there is no principled way to silently pick one, so this refuses); (2) writing

from src.physics.fingerprint.frozen_constants import FINGERPRINT_FROZEN

    Table ``driver_fingerprint_cells``: primary key ``cell_key`` (``NOT NULL``), plus the
    six ``CellAddress`` identity columns, the fitted ``mean``/``sigma``/``support_n``/
    ``shared_floor_applied`` payload, ``status`` (``"resolved"``/``"unresolved"``), and
    ``format_version``.
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH, *, must_exist: bool = False) -> None:
        """Construct the store, creating the schema on first use.

        must_exist:
            When True, raise ``FileNotFoundError`` if ``db_path`` does not already exist,
            BEFORE any connect/schema work -- a read-only construction mode (mirrors
            ``ReferenceUtilizationStore``/``GripStore``).
        """
        if must_exist and not Path(db_path).exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(db_path)
        self.db_path = db_path
        self._init_schema()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ schema
    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        con = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        return con

    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
        parent = Path(self.db_path).parent
        if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
            parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}" TEXT NOT NULL' if c == "cell_key" else f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
        with self._connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}, "
                f'PRIMARY KEY ("cell_key"))'
            )
            self._migrate_missing_columns(con)

    def _migrate_missing_columns(self, con: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        """ALTER-add any expected column absent from an existing table (additive only).

        Mirrors the house pattern exactly: a DB created before a new nullable column was
        added keeps loading -- the ADD COLUMN backfills existing rows with NULL rather than
        crashing the query. Never drops or renames.
        """
        existing = {row[1] for row in con.execute("PRAGMA table_info(driver_fingerprint_cells)")}
        for c in _COLUMNS:
            if c not in existing:
                con.execute(f'ALTER TABLE driver_fingerprint_cells ADD COLUMN "{c}"')

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ guards
    def _check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(self, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary) -> None:
        if era != vocabulary.rules_era:
            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
                f"era={era!r} does not match vocabulary.rules_era={vocabulary.rules_era!r} "
                f"(vocabulary_id={vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r}) -- refusing rather than "
                f"silently choosing one"
            )

    def _check_no_vocabulary_drift(
        self, con: sqlite3.Connection, driver: str, era: str, channel: str, what_measure: str,
        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
    ) -> None:
        existing = {
            row[0]
            for row in con.execute(
                "SELECT DISTINCT vocabulary_version FROM driver_fingerprint_cells "
                "WHERE driver=? AND era=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, channel, what_measure),
            )
        }
        stale = existing - {vocabulary.vocabulary_id}
        if stale:
            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
                f"driver={driver!r} era={era!r} channel={channel!r} what_measure={what_measure!r} "
                f"already has stored cells under vocabulary_version(s) {sorted(stale)!r} -- "
                f"refusing to write under a different vocabulary_version "
                f"{vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r} without an explicit migration"
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write
    def write_fingerprint(
        self,
        driver: str,
        era: str,
        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
        channel: str,
        what_measure: str,
        observations: Mapping[str, CellObservation],
        *,
        allow_unverified: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Write EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` rows, one per ``vocabulary.class_ids``.

        A class absent from ``observations``, or whose ``support_n`` is below the
        pre-registered unresolved-support floor, is written as ``status="unresolved"``
        (``NULL`` mean/sigma) -- never a missing row. ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` on the
        non-NULL ``cell_key`` primary key makes a rerun idempotent (replace-on-rerun):
        re-writing the same fingerprint never accumulates duplicate rows.
        """
        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
        if what_measure in RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES:
            raise ReservedWhatMeasureError(
                f"what_measure={what_measure!r} is a reserved (Build-2, dormant) slot -- "
                f"the store refuses to populate it in Build 1"
            )
        vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)

        placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in _COLUMNS)
        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
        sql = f"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}) VALUES ({placeholders})"

        rows: list[tuple] = []
        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
            obs = observations.get(class_id)
            support_n = obs.support_n if obs is not None else None
            is_resolved = (
                obs is not None
                and support_n is not None
                and support_n >= _UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR
            )
            address = CellAddress(
                driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
                class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
            )
            rows.append(
                (
                    address.cell_key, driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, class_id, channel,
                    what_measure,
                    (obs.mean if is_resolved else None),
                    (obs.sigma if is_resolved else None),
                    support_n,
                    (_RESOLVED if is_resolved else _UNRESOLVED),
                    (obs.shared_floor_applied if obs is not None else None),
                    FORMAT_VERSION,
                )
            )

        with self._connect() as con:
            self._check_no_vocabulary_drift(con, driver, era, channel, what_measure, vocabulary)
            con.executemany(sql, rows)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ reads
    def get_fingerprint(
        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
    ) -> list[FingerprintCell]:
        """Return EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` cells -- never fits, never omits a class.

        A class with no stored row is synthesized as an ``"unresolved"`` cell purely by
        enumerating ``vocabulary.class_ids`` -- no observation is read, no value is
        computed. This is the NO-fit-on-read guarantee: a miss is a placeholder, not a
        trigger.
        """
        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
        with self._connect() as con:
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
            ).fetchall()
        by_class = {r["class_id"]: r for r in rows}

        cells: list[FingerprintCell] = []
        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
            row = by_class.get(class_id)
            if row is None:
                cells.append(
                    FingerprintCell(
                        driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
                        class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
                        mean=None, sigma=None, support_n=None, status=_UNRESOLVED,
                        shared_floor_applied=None, format_version=FORMAT_VERSION,
                    )
                )
            else:
                cells.append(
                    FingerprintCell(
                        driver=row["driver"], era=row["era"], vocabulary_version=row["vocabulary_version"],
                        class_id=row["class_id"], channel=row["channel"], what_measure=row["what_measure"],
                        mean=row["mean"], sigma=row["sigma"], support_n=row["support_n"],
                        status=row["status"], shared_floor_applied=row["shared_floor_applied"],
                        format_version=row["format_version"],
                    )
                )
        return cells

    def row_count(
        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
    ) -> int:
        """Number of stored rows for this (driver,era,vocab,channel,what_measure) slot.

        Diagnostic -- used by idempotency tests to confirm a rerun never accumulates
        duplicate rows (expected to equal ``vocabulary.k`` after any number of rewrites).
        """
        with self._connect() as con:
            cur = con.execute(
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
            )
            return int(cur.fetchone()[0])

11

13	`pool_random_effects`) on top of the driver x class two-way decomposition. That decision
14	must rest on a POWERED, non-circular coverage measurement -- not eyeballing one fit on
15	one real (tiny) slice. This module reproduces #665's synthetic-recovery method
16	(``scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py``, READ-ONLY, not edited here) but swaps
17	#665's PROXY class-share profiles for the REAL per-(driver, class) support counts read
18	from the commander-provided bounded slice DB -- the actual imbalance the G3 fit will see.
19	
20	## Method (PRIMARY verdict)
21	
22	For each channel (`time`: `time_deficit_s`, `energy`: `deployment_share`) and axis

26	   the slice (the actual cell imbalance the G3 fit sees). A cell whose summed support
27	   falls below ``FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR`` (pre-registered, #666
28	   ``frozen_constants.py``) is `unresolved` and excluded (no synthetic draws for it --
29	   same "legitimate empty cell" convention #665 uses for a `n <= 0` cell).
30	2. Generative model (#665's, reused verbatim in structure):
31	   `y[d,c] = grand_mean + true_driver_effect[d] + true_class_effect[c] + N(0, obs_sigma)`,
32	   fresh `true_driver_effect ~ N(0, driver_sigma)` / `true_class_effect ~ N(0,
33	   class_sigma)` drawn each repetition. TIME-channel sigmas are #665's own constants
34	   verbatim (`driver_sigma=0.15, class_sigma=0.30, obs_sigma=1.0`). ENERGY-channel sigmas
35	   are these same three values scaled by ``ENERGY_SCALE`` -- see "Energy-channel sigma

37	   commander-pre-registered).

39	   `src.physics.layer2.pooling` (never edited by this module). Each shrunk axis effect is
40	   wrapped in `predictive_t(eff, sem, n_eff, nu_loss=4.0, rule=FormulaRule())` where `sem`
41	   is the naive (unshrunk) within-group SEM (`fit_two_way` exposes no per-effect sigma of
42	   its own -- same companion-sigma construction #665 uses) and `n_eff` is the SUMMED REAL
43	   observation count backing that axis estimate (driver: sum over that driver's resolved
44	   cells; class: sum over that class's resolved cells) -- **never** `fit_two_way`'s own
45	   `.n` (a total-row count, not a per-axis effective count; #665's exact subtlety).

47	   true_val <= hi)`. Accumulated over `N_REPS >= 200` repetitions x every entity present

"""#675 class-axis coverage diagnostic: does the driver x class two-way `predictive_t`
interval under-cover on the CLASS axis on REAL bounded-slice support, and does that
under-coverage generalize across BOTH channels (time, energy)?

Epic #659 gate 666-g1-implement (research diagnostic; test-after/inspection per the
handoff test mode -- NOT promoted logic). See
``.agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/crew-handoffs/g1-implement-handoff.md`` for the
full pre-registered coverage method this module pins EXACTLY.

## Why this exists

The G3 fit needs to know whether to apply a class-level `shared_floor` (#627 G4,
`pool_random_effects`) on top of the driver x class two-way decomposition. That decision
must rest on a POWERED, non-circular coverage measurement -- not eyeballing one fit on
one real (tiny) slice. This module reproduces #665's synthetic-recovery method
(``scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py``, READ-ONLY, not edited here) but swaps
#665's PROXY class-share profiles for the REAL per-(driver, class) support counts read
from the commander-provided bounded slice DB -- the actual imbalance the G3 fit will see.

## Method (PRIMARY verdict)

For each channel (`time`: `time_deficit_s`, `energy`: `deployment_share`) and axis
(`driver`, `class`):

1. Real per-(driver, class) SUPPORT COUNTS: `n_points` summed across the 4 circuits in
   the slice (the actual cell imbalance the G3 fit sees). A cell whose summed support
   falls below ``FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR`` (pre-registered, #666
   ``frozen_constants.py``) is `unresolved` and excluded (no synthetic draws for it --
   same "legitimate empty cell" convention #665 uses for a `n <= 0` cell).
2. Generative model (#665's, reused verbatim in structure):
   `y[d,c] = grand_mean + true_driver_effect[d] + true_class_effect[c] + N(0, obs_sigma)`,
   fresh `true_driver_effect ~ N(0, driver_sigma)` / `true_class_effect ~ N(0,
   class_sigma)` drawn each repetition. TIME-channel sigmas are #665's own constants
   verbatim (`driver_sigma=0.15, class_sigma=0.30, obs_sigma=1.0`). ENERGY-channel sigmas
   are these same three values scaled by ``ENERGY_SCALE`` -- see "Energy-channel sigma
   derivation" below (an implementer choice, per the handoff's Authority section; NOT
   commander-pre-registered).
3. `fit_two_way(values, teams=drivers, circuits=classes)` -- UNMODIFIED import from
   `src.physics.layer2.pooling` (never edited by this module). Each shrunk axis effect is
   wrapped in `predictive_t(eff, sem, n_eff, nu_loss=4.0, rule=FormulaRule())` where `sem`
   is the naive (unshrunk) within-group SEM (`fit_two_way` exposes no per-effect sigma of
   its own -- same companion-sigma construction #665 uses) and `n_eff` is the SUMMED REAL
   observation count backing that axis estimate (driver: sum over that driver's resolved
   cells; class: sum over that class's resolved cells) -- **never** `fit_two_way`'s own
   `.n` (a total-row count, not a per-axis effective count; #665's exact subtlety).
4. `lo, hi = pt.interval(FINGERPRINT_NOMINAL_COVERAGE_LEVEL)` (0.80); `hit = int(lo <=
   true_val <= hi)`. Accumulated over `N_REPS >= 200` repetitions x every entity present
   in that repetition, per axis per channel.
5. Empirical coverage = hits / n, reported WITH a Clopper-Pearson exact 95% binomial CI
   (so the `generalizes` flag below does not flip on sampling noise alone).

estimate does.

rows (severity classes only) -- preserves the SAME relative structure #665 uses
(`driver_sigma : class_sigma : obs_sigma = 0.15 : 0.30 : 1.0`) rescaled to the energy
channel's own real magnitude, rather than reusing the time-channel's absolute sigmas on a
~20x-smaller-spread quantity (which would trivially inflate coverage). This is a fixed,
STATED, data-independent-of-outcome scaling (it only touches the channel's own overall
spread, never anything about coverage) -- computed once from the real rows, then held
fixed across all `N_REPS` repetitions, exactly mirroring how #665 fixes its sigmas before

263	def gate_fingerprint(cells_by_dc: Mapping[tuple[str, str], "list"], k: int) -> GatingVerdict:
264	    """Critic #3 non-empty/finite gating for G.
265	
266	    FAILS (not a vacuous pass) when: no cells at all; any (driver, channel) does
267	    not carry exactly ``k`` cells; any *resolved* cell has a non-finite mean/sigma;
268	    or every cell is unresolved (no signal recovered anywhere).
269	    """
270	    if not cells_by_dc:
271	        return GatingVerdict(False, {"n_groups": 0}, "no fingerprint cells written")
272	    n_cells = 0
273	    n_resolved = 0
274	    problems: list[str] = []
275	    for (driver, channel), cells in cells_by_dc.items():
276	        if len(cells) != k:
277	            problems.append(f"{driver}/{channel}: {len(cells)} cells != k={k}")
278	            continue
279	        for c in cells:
280	            n_cells += 1
281	            if getattr(c, "status", None) == "resolved":
282	                n_resolved += 1
283	                if not (is_finite_number(c.mean) and is_finite_number(c.sigma)):
284	                    problems.append(
285	                        f"{driver}/{channel}/{c.class_id}: resolved but non-finite "
286	                        f"mean={c.mean!r} sigma={c.sigma!r}"
287	                    )
288	    if n_resolved == 0:
289	        problems.append("no resolved cells anywhere (vacuous)")
290	    passed = not problems
291	    return GatingVerdict(
292	        passed,
293	        {"n_groups": len(cells_by_dc), "n_cells": n_cells, "n_resolved": n_resolved, "k": k},
294	        "; ".join(problems) if problems else "k cells per group, resolved finite",

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Public entry point
def fit_driver_fingerprints(
    observables_db_path: str,
    store: DriverFingerprintStore,
    driver: str,
    *,
    as_of_round: int,
    era: str,
    vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
    season: int,
    session_type: str = "Q",
    map_version: Optional[str] = None,
    channels: Sequence[str] = FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS,
    what_measure: str = DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE,
    allow_unverified: bool = False,
) -> Mapping[str, Mapping[str, CellObservation]]:
    """Fit one driver's fingerprint cells (both channels) as-of ``as_of_round`` and write
    them into ``store``.

    ``as_of_round`` is keyword-only with NO default -- a call that omits it raises
    ``TypeError`` from Python's own argument binding, before a single line of this function
    body runs (crown invariant "as_of_round REQUIRED no default").

    Refuses via ``vocabulary.require_fittable()`` unless the taxonomy's F12 verdict is
    ``"PASS"`` (or ``allow_unverified=True``), mirroring ``store.write_fingerprint``'s own
    refusal. Writes exactly ``vocabulary.k`` cells per channel via
    ``store.write_fingerprint`` -- a class with no in-cutoff support (or below the
    pre-registered support floor) is written ``"unresolved"`` by the store itself, never a
    missing row.

    Returns the RESOLVED observations actually computed per channel (a diagnostic /
    test-facing return value; the store write is the durable side effect).
    """
    vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)

    rows = _read_observable_rows(
        observables_db_path, season=season, session_type=session_type,
        map_version=map_version, as_of_round=as_of_round,
    )

    written: dict[str, dict[str, CellObservation]] = {}
    for channel in channels:
        if channel not in _VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL:
            raise ValueError(
                f"channel: expected one of {sorted(_VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL)}, got {channel!r}"
            )
        observations = _fit_channel(
            rows, channel, driver=driver, as_of_round=as_of_round,
            halflife_rounds=_RECENCY_HALFLIFE_ROUNDS, unresolved_floor=_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR,
            class_ids=vocabulary.class_ids,
        )
        store.write_fingerprint(
            driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure, observations,
            allow_unverified=allow_unverified,
        )
        written[channel] = observations
    return written

# cmdr-698 — Problem Statement

**Issue:** #698 — #666 follow-on hardening: store-API primitive-obsession, script `.pth` path, gitignore.
**Engagement:** PLANNING ONLY. No source/test/doc edits, no commit/push/PR, no issue comment.
**Interrogation:** `.agent-work/cmdr-698/INTERROGATION_RECORD.json` (8 questions, rail exit 0, instructed self-sign-off).

## The ask, in behavior terms

Three independent hardening items over the `src/physics/fingerprint/` package (#666, epic #659 stage G).
None blocked the #666 merge; all are recommend-and-defer debt now being paid.

**H1 — the real work.** Today `DriverFingerprintStore`'s three public methods
(`write_fingerprint`, `get_fingerprint`, `row_count`, `store.py:193/255/298`) take four bare
`str` identity arguments plus a `ClassVocabulary`. The six-field validation that `CellAddress`
performs (`address.py:88-104`: non-empty `str`, no `|` delimiter, known `what_measure`) is
reached only at `store.py:233` — **inside** the per-class write loop, after the store has already
committed to a row set — and on the read path is never reached at all. After H1, an ill-formed
identity is refused **at the call**, before any store work.

**H2.** `scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py` lacks the worktree-first `sys.path` insertion its
three sibling scripts have, so a bare direct-file run inside a git worktree resolves
`from src.physics...` against the MAIN checkout via the editable-install `.pth`.

**H3.** Confirm no regenerable artifact from this family lands in a tracked path on a non-epic run.

## Two premises I was handed that are false

Both were checked against source rather than accepted, and both change what the plan does.

1. **H1's acceptance wording is unattainable as literally written.** `CellAddress` has six fields
   and addresses **one cell**; the store's unit of work is the **k-cell group**. `class_id` is the
   fan-out axis (`store.py:225`, `:275`) and `vocabulary_version` is read off the vocabulary
   (`store.py:234`), so neither is a store argument. Passing a `CellAddress` with a sentinel
   `class_id` would violate the value object's own documented invariant. The honest target is the
   address **prefix** — which `store.py`'s own docstring already calls a *slot* (`:22-23`, `:186`, `:301`).

2. **H3's premise "already ignored via `.agent-work/`" is false.** `.gitignore` carries no
   `.agent-work/` rule; the tree is **deliberately tracked** (engine-config `rules_root`: commit
   Commander logs once archived), and the #666 artifacts are committed on purpose. The real
   exposure is elsewhere — see below.

A third correction, found while sizing the blast radius: `docs/architecture/packets/physics.md:2753`
says `instrument_panel` "reads `fingerprint.store.get_fingerprint` cells directly." Against source
that is **false as a call claim** — no `instrument_panel` module or its report script references the
store at all. The panel *receives* cells; the pilot fetches them. Read literally it would have sent
an implementer hunting a call site that does not exist.

## Rulings (no human reachable; recorded, decided, and graded)

- **Slot shape.** Frozen `FingerprintSlot(driver, era, channel, what_measure)` in `address.py`
  beside `CellAddress`, sharing its exact validator, exposing
  `address_for(class_id, vocabulary) -> CellAddress` as the sole `CellAddress` constructor on the
  store path. `ClassVocabulary` stays the single authority for `vocabulary_version` + `class_ids`.
  Rejected: a per-cell API (destroys the k-cells-always-populated and no-fit-on-read invariants,
  which are #666 Protected Intent and live *in* the fan-out); a slot that also carries
  `vocabulary_version` (asserts it twice, buys nothing, costs a second refusal path).
  `@grade: settled/inherited` for the shape; `@grade: guess` for the name alone.
- **Tightening.** CellAddress parity only. **No** channel-set membership check — `CellAddress`
  never enforces `FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` either, and `fit.py:347-350` already validates channel
  independently → triage. The dormant reserved `what_measure` slot stays **constructible but
  refused at write** (epic #659 ruling 4; `test_store.py:153-161` asserts the error type).
  Slot construction stays **vocabulary-blind** so era disagreement keeps raising
  `EraVocabularyMismatchError`, not a construction `ValueError`. `@grade: settled/inherited`.
- **Evidence.** Scoped to the closed importer set, never a blanket suite
  (`lesson:scope-self-authored-regression-to-import-graph`). Store is a consumed frozen module, so
  its own pre-existing tests re-run with every refusal raising the **same** exception type
  (`lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`). `@grade: settled/inherited`.

## Protected intent — what must not move

The four keystone invariants stated at `store.py:10-32`: non-NULL `cell_key`; k-cells-always-populated;
loud refusal with no silent substitution; **no fit-on-read**. Plus every number `fit.py` produces —
this is a type/seam refactor, so no `mean`, `sigma`, `support_n`, `status`, or coverage verdict changes.
`constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` continues to hold (nothing here reaches toward evo).

## Blast radius (closed by grep over `src/ scripts/ tests/`)

| Kind | Site |
|---|---|
| production writer | `src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:356` (the only writer anywhere) |
| production readers | `src/physics/pilot/pipeline.py:257`, `:325` |
| scripts | `scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:124`, `scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py:173` |
| tests | `test_store.py` (~20 sites), `test_fit.py:160`, `test_bounded_validation.py:173,:267,:326,:333` |
| **not** affected | `instrument_panel/*` (never touches the store), `fingerprint/__init__.py` (re-exports nothing) |

## H3, reframed to what is actually exposed

- **`data/driver_fingerprint.db`** (`store.py:50` `DEFAULT_DB_PATH`) is **absent from `.gitignore`**,
  while every sibling own-DB is present (`/data/reference_utilization.db` #664,
  `/data/segment_maps.db` #662, `/data/driver_utility_observables.db` + `/data/driver_utility.db` #628).
  A default-path fit run drops an untracked **binary SQLite DB** into `data/` — precisely the artifact
  class the archive step's own deny-globs exist to stop. This is the highest-value item in H3 and the
  issue's JSON framing missed it.
- Three scripts write regenerable JSON to hardcoded **live** `.agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/`
  paths with no `--out` flag (`fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py:123` — argparse at `:472-473` offers
  only `--slice-db`/`--n-reps`; `fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:48`; `join_bounded_validation_667.py:70`).
  A re-run outside an epic work area stages them under `git add -A`.

## Out of scope

Any behavior change to the fit or the coverage diagnostic (issue's own exclusion). Channel-set
enforcement. Adding `--out` flags to the three scripts. Rewriting the store to a per-cell API.
Correcting the `instrument_panel` packet prose (reconcile/triage, not a code gate).

RAIL: A working solution is the MIDDLE of this run — you are 7 steps from done. Next: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the map input the context step resolved, using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). Write it to .agent-work/cmdr-698/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Know what that check is and is not, and do not overclaim it: it is a regression floor so map-IGNORING cannot silently return, not the fix for map-LATENESS. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. # Mission Frame — cmdr-698

Map-first frame for issue #698 (#666 follow-on hardening). Authored from the map input the
`context` step resolved (RESOLVED, entrypoint `docs/architecture/index.md`, 76 anchors, receipt
`.agent-work/cmdr-698/map-orientation.json`) **before** any source read.

Not skipped as trivial: H1 changes the public read/write surface of a **keystone state store**
whose invariants the map records other components as trusting, so the map genuinely constrains
the plan — most sharply by carrying **one claim about this area that is false against source**.

## Intent

Move the DriverFingerprint cell store's identity arguments from loose primitives onto a validated
value object, so a structurally ill-formed address is refused **at the call** rather than reaching
the row-write loop — without moving a single fitted number, and without disturbing any of the four
keystone invariants `struct:physics.fingerprint` publishes to its consumers. Plus two isolated
hygiene fixes (a script `sys.path` guard, a `.gitignore` omission) with no runtime coupling to it.

## Affected Capabilities

- **Fingerprint cell persistence + retrieval** (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `store.py`) — today
  keys three public methods on four bare `str` + a `ClassVocabulary`; after this run, on a validated
  slot value object. Behavior of what is stored/returned is unchanged.
- **Fingerprint fitting** (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `fit.py`) — the sole writer; it only
  changes how it *names* the write target. `purpose:weekend_utilization_prior` is downstream and
  untouched.
- **Pilot orchestration** (`struct:physics.pilot`, `purpose:pilot_orchestration`) — the only
  production *reader*; two call sites re-typed, no logic change.
- **Class-axis coverage diagnostic** (`scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py`) — gains an
  import guard only; its verdict math is explicitly out of scope.

## Examples / Events

- A caller passing `what_measure="banana"` today gets rows written under a nonsense measure; after
  this run it raises at slot construction. This is the acceptance H1 asks for, and no current
  caller does it.
- A caller passing a **reserved** measure (`"push"`, `"managed"`, …) must **still construct fine**
  and be refused only at write — epic #659 ruling 4's present-but-unused dormant slot. Edge case
  that a naive "validate everything at construction" implementation silently breaks.
- A caller passing an `era` that disagrees with `vocabulary.rules_era` must still raise
  `EraVocabularyMismatchError`, not a construction `ValueError` — so the slot stays vocabulary-blind.
- Running `py scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py` from a git worktree today resolves
  `src.*` against the MAIN checkout via the editable-install `.pth`; pytest never sees this because
  it inserts its own root.

## Structural Anchors

- `struct:physics.fingerprint` — `src/physics/fingerprint/`, component. Owns `address.py`
  (`CellAddress`), `store.py` (`DriverFingerprintStore`, `FingerprintCell`), `fit.py`,
  `vocabulary.py`, `join.py`. **All H1 code lands here.**
- `struct:physics.pilot` — `src/physics/pilot/`, component. Pure consumer; the two `get_fingerprint`
  call sites at `pipeline.py:257`/`:325`.
- `struct:physics.instrument_panel` — `src/physics/instrument_panel/`, component. **Verified NOT a
  caller** (see Disputes); no change.
- `struct:physics` — parent container; the region boundary this run stays inside.

## Governing Constraints / Assumptions

- `constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` — nothing in `src/physics/` may import evo /
  `latent_power` / `compound_prior`. This run adds no import at all beyond intra-package, so the
  constraint is preserved trivially; the reviewer still re-verifies rather than assuming.
- **Assumption (project doctrine, `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md`):** physics is a *rigorous*
  region — test-led change, focused region suite, `simplification_limits` on touched paths.
  `address.py` gains a dataclass, so the file-length limit is a live concern, not a formality.
- **Assumption (`store.py:10-32`, #666 Protected Intent):** the four keystone invariants —
  non-NULL `cell_key`, k-cells-always-populated, loud refusal with no silent substitution, no
  fit-on-read — are what every downstream consumer trusts. A per-cell API would destroy two of them.

## Decision Anchors & Decision Pressure

- `decision:join-consumer-boundary` — the join is for practice-update/fusion summaries; the race
  sim and the panel read **un-aggregated cells**, not the aggregate. Constrains this run only in
  that the un-aggregated read path (`get_fingerprint`) must keep working identically for both.
  `@grade: settled/inherited · leans g1-slot,g2-callers`
- `decision:fingerprint-slot-is-the-address-prefix` (**new, this run**) — the store API is typed on
  a frozen `FingerprintSlot(driver, era, channel, what_measure)`, not on `CellAddress`, because the
  store addresses a k-cell group while `CellAddress` addresses one cell. `ClassVocabulary` remains
  the single authority for `vocabulary_version` and `class_ids`.
  `@grade: settled/inherited · leans g1-slot · ` the group shape follows from #666 Protected Intent,
  not from this run's preference; the **name** alone is `@grade: guess` and freely revisable.
- `decision:slot-validation-is-cellAddress-parity` (**new, this run**) — the slot shares
  `CellAddress`'s exact validator; no channel-set membership check; reserved measures stay
  constructible-but-refused-at-write.
  `@grade: settled/inherited · leans g1-slot,g3-tests`
- **Decision pressure (surfaced, not taken):** should `CellAddress`/`FingerprintSlot` enforce
  `channel in FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS`? Deferred — it is a genuine behavior tightening with its own
  blast radius (hard-wires the constant against a future third channel) and `fit.py:347-350`
  already validates channel independently. Routed to triage.
- **Decision pressure (surfaced, not taken):** should the three fingerprint scripts take `--out`
  instead of hardcoding `.agent-work/...` paths? Deferred — it is an interface change, not
  hygiene. Routed to triage.

## Claims / Evidence Surfaces

- `claim:instrument_panel_reads_cells_directly` — **DISPUTED by this run**; see below.
- `claim:pilot-runs-end-to-end-3-circuits` — the pilot's end-to-end run over Monaco/Belgium/GB
  2023-Q exercises both `get_fingerprint` call sites. Not re-run here (it needs real telemetry);
  the scoped `tests/unit/physics/pilot` suite is the standing proxy, and the gate says so honestly
  rather than implying the real pilot was re-run.
- Evidence each gate re-confirms: the store's own pre-existing test files pass **unmodified in
  intent**, with every refusal raising the *same* exception type as before
  (`lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`); `simplification_limits` clean on touched paths.

## Map Confidence / Staleness / Disputes

- **`claim:instrument_panel_reads_cells_directly` — DISPUTED.**

# cmdr-698 — Plan decisions, alternatives, and critic

Companion to `execute.json`. Records the two principal-governed rigor mechanisms the `plan` step
owes (plan-alternatives c4, cold plan critic c5), the untaken roads, and the residual risks a
returning human should see before approving.

---

## Session constraint that shapes both mechanisms

This session carries an explicit standing instruction: **do not call the Agent tool unless the user
requested it**, and the user did not. Both rigor mechanisms are normally *parallel subagent* work.
I therefore ran both **in-context**, and I am labelling exactly what that does and does not buy
rather than claiming a pass I did not earn. Doctrine's escape here is bias-to-yes with any skip
**surfaced as a named untaken road** — that is what this file is.

---

## Plan-alternatives (c4) — RUN, in-context, single author

Three gate-plan candidates generated under **distinct named constraints**, then compared and
converged to one recommendation (not a menu).

### Candidate A — constraint: *fewest gates, cheapest run*
One gate: H1 + H2 + H3 in a single implement/review/integrate cycle.

- **Depth:** poor. One reviewer holds a keystone-store signature change, an import-path fix and a
  gitignore line in one head; the store change is the only risky part and it gets diluted.
- **Locality:** poor. A BLOCK on the trivial gitignore line reopens the store work.
- **Testability:** poor. One verdict over three unrelated evidence shapes (a scoped pytest, a bare
  direct-file import proof, and `git check-ignore` exit codes).
- **Verdict:** rejected. Cheapness is not the binding constraint on a 3-item hardening issue.

### Candidate B — constraint: *green at every gate boundary, smallest reasonable bite*
g1 additive value object → g2 atomic re-type + all callers → g3 hygiene.

- **Depth:** good. g1 isolates the subtle semantics (parity validation, the dormant reserved-measure
  slot) with **zero** callers at risk, so if that reasoning is wrong it is caught while the tree is
  still green. g2 is then a mechanical signature move over an already-proven object.
- **Locality:** good. Each gate's BLOCK surface is disjoint.
- **Seam placement:** g1 places the seam in `address.py` beside `CellAddress`, one file owning the
  whole identity space; g2 merely consumes it.
- **Testability:** good. Three distinct, honest evidence shapes, one per gate.
- **Why g2 must stay atomic:** a signature change with its callers split across gates leaves a
  known-red window bridged by waivers — the doctrine calls that a plan smell, and it would cost a
  human waiver per gate plus a "prove the red is benign" detour in every review.
- **Verdict:** **recommended.**

### Candidate C — constraint: *diagnose before fixing; prove no numbers moved*
g0 evidence-only harness that snapshots written rows before the change, then g1/g2/g3 as in B, with
g2 closing on a before/after row-equality assertion.

- **Depth:** highest confidence on the "no behavior change" claim, which is the issue's own stated
  boundary and the thing a green suite does **not** actually prove.
- **Cost:** a whole extra crew gate for a refactor where every value is carried through untouched by
  construction (the slot only renames how the write target is addressed).
- **Verdict:** rejected as a standalone gate, **but its central idea is grafted into B** — g2's
  evidence anchors now require a same-inputs before/after row-equality check
  (`cell_key`/`mean`/`sigma`/`support_n`/`status`), and `g2-review` item (c) explicitly forbids the
  reviewer from accepting "the suite is green" as proof of numeric identity.

**Converged recommendation: Candidate B with C's row-equality evidence grafted in.** That is what
`execute.json` encodes.

### Untaken road (named)
The **parallel multi-agent** form of design-it-twice — independent authors under separate
constraints with no sight of each other. Not run: agent dispatch is barred this session. What that
costs is real and worth stating: candidates written by one author share that author's blind spots,
so the comparison above is a genuine structured comparison but **not** an independence check.

---

## Cold plan critic (c5) — RUN in-context, and explicitly NOT COLD

A cold critic reads the plan and frame *only*, with no authoring context. I authored both, so this
is an adversarial self-read and I am not going to dress it up as more. Findings I could not dismiss:

1. **A check that could not fail (FIXED).** `g2-integrate.c2` was originally a negative `grep` over
   the store's signature block. That formulation passes **vacuously** when the methods are absent or
   renamed — precisely the failure it exists to catch. Rewritten as an AST parse that raises on a
   missing class or method, and then **dry-run against the unmodified tree, where it exited 1 and
   named all three methods**. A check nobody has watched fail is not evidence.
2. **The interpreter trap (RECORDED as a residual risk).** The first draft of that check imported
   `DriverFingerprintStore`; `src/physics/__init__.py:52` pulls `scipy`, which is missing from some
   agent shells. It failed on the spot when dry-run. The rewritten check is import-free, but
   `g1/g2-integrate`'s pytest and `simplification_limits` commands **do** need the full interpreter —
   see residual risks below.
3. **The `claim:pilot-runs-end-to-end-3-circuits` proxy.** g2 changes both pilot read sites but does
   not re-run the real 3-circuit pilot (it needs real telemetry). The plan says so out loud in g2's
   evidence anchors rather than letting a green unit suite imply the real pathway was exercised.
4. **g3 bundles two unrelated fixes.** Defensible — both are single-file, zero-risk, and one crew
   pass covers them — but each keeps its **own** close criterion, so a failure is attributable.
5. **Residual, accepted:** `pyright` is not a gate here. The repo has a baseline-diff CI gate (#545)
   and a signature change can move that baseline. It is not in `ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT`'s evidence
   table and its checks are non-required, so it stays a named risk rather than a fourth gate.

### Untaken road (named)
A **genuine cold critic** — an agent handed only `execute.json` + `MISSION_FRAME.md` with no
authoring context, and for a plan touching a keystone store arguably a 3-lens panel
(intent-fit / testability / simplicity). Not run: agent dispatch is barred this session. This is the
**larger** of the two gaps, because self-critique cannot find the assumptions I do not know I made.
**Recommendation to the returning human: run this before execute begins.** It is cheap relative to
the store's blast radius.

---

## Residual risks a human should see before approving

- **Interpreter environment.** The `execute` engagement must drive the engine from a shell whose
  `py` resolves to the full `pythoncore-3.14-64` install. The Bash-tool `py` lacks `scipy`
  (confirmed live this run), and `g1/g2-integrate`'s pytest postconditions import `src.physics`.
  A wrong shell makes every physics gate fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the change.
- **`git check-ignore` availability.** `g3-integrate.c2` shells out to git; it was not dry-run here
  because the permission layer declined those invocations during planning. The command is standard
  and the control-path arm makes it non-vacuous, but it is the one check in this plan that has
  **not** been observed running.
- **Two of the three ratifying decisions are mine, not a human's** (slot shape, tightening scope).
  Both are graded `settled/inherited` because they follow from #666 Protected Intent rather than my
  preference, and both are recorded verbatim as the question I would have asked — so either can be
  overturned without re-deriving the analysis. The **name** `FingerprintSlot` is graded `guess` and
  is the cheapest thing to change.

---

## Panel-vs-single choice (surfaced, per doctrine)

Weight assessment: this plan touches a keystone state store with a closed, small blast radius and
no new external interface. That sits at the boundary — **single** critic is defensible on blast
radius, **panel** is indicated because it is a keystone store. Doctrine says *when in doubt, panel*.
I could run neither. The choice is therefore surfaced unresolved, with the recommendation above.

## What the investigation changed about the issue

Three things I was handed turned out to be wrong, and each one moved the plan:

**H1's acceptance is unattainable as literally written.** `CellAddress` has six fields and addresses **one cell**; the store addresses a **k-cell group** — `class_id` is the fan-out axis (`store.py:225`, `:275`) and `vocabulary_version` is read off the vocabulary, so neither is a store argument. A `CellAddress` with a sentinel `class_id` would violate the value object's own invariant. The honest target is the address *prefix* — which `store.py`'s own docstring already calls a **slot** (`:22-23`, `:186`, `:301`), so the plan inherits a name instead of coining one.

**H3's premise is false.** `.gitignore` has no `.agent-work/` rule; that tree is *deliberately tracked* (engine-config mandates committing archived Commander logs), and the #666 JSONs are committed on purpose. The real omission the JSON framing missed: `store.py:50`'s `DEFAULT_DB_PATH = 'data/driver_fingerprint.db'` is absent from `.gitignore` while **every** sibling own-DB is listed — a default-path fit run drops an untracked binary SQLite DB into `data/`.

**The architecture map is wrong about this area.** `packets/physics.md:2753` says `instrument_panel` "reads `fingerprint.store.get_fingerprint` cells directly." No module there references the store at all — the panel *receives* cells, the pilot fetches them. Read literally it would have sent an implementer hunting a call site that doesn't exist. `check_arch_map.py` is green over it. The caller set was closed by independent reverse grep instead.

H2 checked out exactly as written: `fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py` is the only one of its four-script family missing the guard.

## Plan shape

Three crew gates, sequenced so the tree is green at every boundary: **g1** adds `FingerprintSlot` to `address.py` purely additively (isolates the subtle semantics — shared validator, and the dormant reserved-`what_measure` slot that must stay *constructible* per epic #659 ruling 4 — with zero callers at risk); **g2** re-types the store and moves all callers **atomically** (splitting a signature change across gates would create a known-red window); **g3** the two hygiene fixes. Evidence is scoped to the closed importer set, never a blanket suite.

I could not dispatch subagents this session, so **no genuine cold plan critic and no independent plan-alternative authors were run**.
